title: Five-Cheese Baked Mac and Cheese
subtitle: Creamy cavatappi with a crispy Parmesan-panko topping
yield: One 8 × 8-inch baking dish; approximately 4–6 side-dish servings
headnote: Alissa Nguyen’s Thanksgiving macaroni and cheese combines sharp cheddar, Monterey Jack, Gruyère, cream cheese and Parmesan. The pasta is finished in a rich milk-and-cream sauce beneath a crunchy cheese and breadcrumb crust.

ingredientGroups.title: Pasta
items: 227 g cavatappi or elbow macaroni (8 oz)
1½ tsp kosher salt, for pasta water

ingredientGroups.title: Cheese blend
items: 227 g sharp cheddar, freshly shredded (8 oz)
113.5 g Monterey Jack, freshly shredded (4 oz)

ingredientGroups.title: Cheese sauce
items: 30 g all-purpose flour (¼ cup, approximate weight)
237 mL heavy whipping cream (1 US cup)
177 mL evaporated milk (6 fl oz; half a 12 fl oz can)

steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a 8 × 8-inch baking dish.
Bring salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta 2 minutes less than the package specifies, drain, and leave unrinsed.
Toss the shredded cheddar, Gruyère and Monterey Jack together. Measure out 1 cup of the mixture for the top; set aside.
In a separate bowl, combine the panko, melted butter, finely grated Parmesan and paprika.
Melt the unsalted butter over medium heat in a large pot. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1–2 minutes.
Gradually whisk the whole milk, heavy cream and evaporated milk into the roux. Add the salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika and mustard powder; simmer 5 minutes.
Lower the heat. Stir in the softened cream cheese, then gradually incorporate the remaining shredded cheese, a handful at a time, until the sauce is smooth.
Fold in the drained pasta and spread in the prepared baking dish. Scatter the reserved shredded cheese over the surface, followed by the panko mixture.
Bake at 375°F, checking at 20 minutes; allow 20–30 minutes, until hot and bubbling. Broil 2–3 minutes until browned, watching closely. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
ingredientNotes: Use freshly grated block cheese rather than packaged pre-shredded cheese for smoother melting.

Make ahead: assemble without the panko mixture, cover and refrigerate the day before. Let stand 30 minutes before baking, add the topping, then bake until hot and bubbling; a chilled casserole may take longer.
Optional source suggestion: add extra cheddar on top for additional browning and cheesiness.
Flour, panko and grated Parmesan weights are approximate volume conversions. All ingredient quantities are halved from the original 9 × 13-inch recipe. Double for the original pan size.
reviewFlags: 8 × 8-inch adaptation not yet family-tested; yield and baking-time range are estimates.
